question: A Spring handler returns a `ProblemDetail` built with `forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.CONFLICT, ...)`. What HTTP status does the client receive?
options: 200, because the handler returned normally
500, because no exception was rethrown
409, because the status stored in the ProblemDetail is used
400, because handlers default to bad request
explanation: Spring sends the status stored in the ProblemDetail, here 409. The body also repeats it in the status member, and the media type is application/problem+json.

question: The server adds `"errors": [...]` to its problem documents. Why does an Angular client that has never heard of that member keep working?
options: RFC 9457 lets servers add members and clients ignore the ones they do not know
HttpClient strips unknown members from every body
TypeScript rejects unknown members at compile time
Spring removes extension members unless the client sends a header
explanation: Extension members are part of the design: a client reads the standard members it needs and ignores the rest. Neither HttpClient nor TypeScript removes anything.

question: A load balancer answers 502 with an empty body. The error handler runs `error.error.errors.map(...)` without a check. What happens?
options: map returns an empty array
A TypeError is thrown inside the handler and the user sees no message
HttpClient converts the empty body into a problem document
The form shows the 502 status as a field error
explanation: With an empty body error.error is null, so reading errors from it throws. A type guard that checks the shape first lets the code fall back to a generic message.

question: After a 400 response, the email field shows the server message 'must be a well-formed email address'. The user fixes the email text. What should happen to that message?
options: It stays until the next successful submit
It stays until the page is reloaded
It is replaced by a validation error with the same text
It disappears, because submission errors clear when the field is edited
explanation: Signal Forms treats a submission error as a one-time server result and clears it when the field changes. Validation rules, by contrast, recompute on each change.

question: The server answers 409 with `{"title":"Conflict","detail":"Email already registered"}` and no `errors` list. Where should the message go?
options: Under the password field, the last one touched
Nowhere, because there is no field to attach it to
As a form-level error returned without a fieldTree
In the browser console only
explanation: The problem is about the whole request, not one named field. An error returned without a fieldTree belongs to the form and can be shown in an alert above the button.
